channel.title: Mazda recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Mazda CX-50 Suspension Bolts May Not Be Tight
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain CX-50 and CX-50 Hybrid vehicles because the bolts that hold the front suspension together may not have been tightened properly during assembly. If these fasteners are too loose, a suspension part or a wheel could come loose from the vehicle.

item.title: Mazda CX-70, CX-90 Fuel Gauge May Read Wrong
item.description: On affected vehicles, the fuel gauge in the instrument cluster may show an inaccurate reading of how much fuel is in the tank. Because the gauge isn't accurate, you could unexpectedly run out of fuel and the vehicle could stall while you are driving.

item.title: Mazda CX-50 Airbag May Deploy Improperly
item.description: On certain CX-50 and CX-50 Hybrid vehicles, the airbag control module software may be set up incorrectly, which can cause the airbag to deploy the wrong way.

item.title: Mazda3 and CX-30 Air Bags May Not Deploy
item.description: Certain Mazda3 and CX-30 vehicles have an air bag problem. The air bag sensor unit may show an error and turn off the air bags if its battery charge gets too low. When the air bags are turned off this way, they will not deploy if the vehicle is in a crash, which increases the risk of injury to people in the vehicle.

item.title: Mazda MX-5 stability control warning light may not illuminate
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain MX-5 models. Because of a software error, the dashboard light for the traction control and stability control systems may not come on when it should. As a result, these cars do not meet the federal safety rule for electronic stability control systems. Dealers will replace the stability control unit.

item.title: Mazda CX-50 Trailer Hitch Bolts May Loosen
item.description: Some Mazda CX-50 vehicles that are equipped with a Mazda genuine accessory trailer hitch have bolts holding the hitch assembly to the vehicle body. These bolts may loosen over time. If they loosen enough, the trailer hitch assembly can come loose and separate from the vehicle body, whether the vehicle is towing a trailer at the time or simply being driven under normal conditions.

item.title: Mazda CX-70 and CX-90 Electrical Unit Software Issue
item.description: In some Mazda CX-90 and CX-70 vehicles equipped with a Dash Electrical Supply Unit, several features may not work correctly during startup. This can affect the defroster, the seat belt warning, the 360-degree view monitor, and, on plug-in hybrid models, the system that cools the high-voltage battery.

item.title: Mazda CX-70 Hybrid Inverter Software May Cut Power
item.description: On these plug-in hybrid vehicles, improper inverter software may cause the malfunction indicator light to come on, and the vehicle may lose drive power while running in electric vehicle mode.

item.title: Mazda CX-70 Control Module Software May Cut Power
item.description: On these vehicles, a software issue in the powertrain control module and engine control module may cause the malfunction indicator light to turn on, and in some cases the vehicle may lose drive power.

item.title: Mazda MX-5 Miata Air Bags May Deploy Too Forcefully
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain MX-5 Miata vehicles. A software error in the control unit that manages the air bags can cause the front air bags to inflate with too much force in a crash. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal safety rule for occupant crash protection. Dealers will update the air bag sensor control software at no cost to the owner. Mazda has already mailed notification letters to owners.

item.title: Mazda Camera Fault May Disable Safety Systems
item.description: On these vehicles, the forward sensing camera can malfunction. When this happens, the automatic emergency braking system and the lane-keep assist system may not work as they are supposed to. In addition, the headlights will not automatically switch from high beams down to low beams the way they are designed to. Because of this, these driver assistance features may fail to function when needed.

item.title: Mazda3 Backup Camera Display May Go Blank
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain 2024 CX-90 and Mazda3 vehicles because a software error may cause the rearview, front, and/or side camera images to not appear on the display. This means the driver may lose the extra view these cameras normally provide. Dealers will update the view monitor control module software to fix the problem.

item.title: Mazda3 and CX-3 Rearview Camera May Malfunction
item.description: Certain 2014 to 2018 Mazda3 and 2016 to 2021 CX-3 vehicles may have a rearview camera that does not display properly. Instead of showing a clear picture, the camera image can flicker or appear distorted. This means the picture you see when using the rearview camera may not be reliable or clear, which can make it harder to see what the camera is supposed to show you behind the vehicle.

item.title: Mazda CX-30, CX-50 Brake Control Unit May Fail
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain CX-30 and CX-50 vehicles because the anti-lock brake system's hydraulic control unit may become damaged. If this happens, the brakes may not work as well as they should, giving the vehicle reduced braking ability. That means it could take a longer distance than normal to slow down and come to a complete stop when needed.

item.title: Mazda CX-50 Trailer Hitch Wiring May Detach
item.description: Certain 2023 Mazda CX-50 vehicles equipped with a Mazda Genuine Accessory trailer hitch have a wiring harness that may come loose and get damaged. This harness powers the lights and brakes on a trailer you're towing. If it fails, the trailer's lights or brakes may stop working while you're driving with a trailer attached.

item.title: Mazda Fuel Pump May Fail and Stall Engine
item.description: The impeller inside the low-pressure fuel pump may crack and become deformed, which can cause the fuel pump to fail. If the pump fails while you are driving, the engine may stall, and stalling increases the risk of a crash. Dealers will replace the fuel pump in affected vehicles, free of charge.

item.title: Mazda CX-9 second-row seat may slide forward in crash
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain CX-9 vehicles that have the 60/40 split bench second-row seats. The left-side second-row seat may unexpectedly slide forward during a crash. Federal safety rules cover how seat belt anchorages must hold, and these vehicles do not meet that standard. A dealer will replace the internal parts inside the affected second-row seats at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Mazda3 and CX-30 Tire Valves May Leak Air
item.description: In some Mazda3 and CX-30 vehicles, air may suddenly leak from a tire's air valve.

item.title: Mazda CX-30 power liftgate may lower on its own
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain CX-30 vehicles. When the power liftgate — the rear hatch that opens and closes by itself — is fully open, it may partially come down on its own if the vehicle is parked facing uphill on a slope. Dealers will update the software that controls the liftgate and check the serial number of the liftgate drive unit, replacing that part if needed. The work is done at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Mazda CX-30 Fuel Hose May Leak Fuel
item.description: Some all-wheel-drive CX-30 vehicles have a fuel tank evaporative vent hose that may become disconnected. When this happens, fuel can leak from the charcoal canister vent located near the back of the vehicle. Mazda dealers will inspect the vent hose, reconnect it if it's disconnected, and replace the charcoal canister along with some related parts, all free of charge to owners.

item.title: Mazda CX-30/Mazda3 Front Brake Caliper Bolts Loose
item.description: On certain Mazda CX-30 and Mazda3 vehicles, the bolts that hold the front brake calipers in place may not have been tightened properly when the vehicle was built. Over time, this can let the calipers become loose. Loose calipers can reduce how well the brakes work or interfere with the wheels turning properly, which affects how the vehicle handles. Either of these problems can increase the risk of a crash.

item.title: Mazda3 automatic braking may stop the car unexpectedly
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain Mazda3 vehicles. The Smart Brake System, which brakes on its own to avoid hitting something, can wrongly sense an object while you are driving and bring the car to a sudden stop. Dealers will update the software for this system. Vehicles built on certain dates will also get an instrument cluster software update or a new cluster, along with a replacement owner's manual. All of this work is free.

item.title: Mazda CX-9 Tires May Lose Tread While Driving
item.description: Some CX-9 SUVs were built with specific Sumitomo Falken tires that may have been manufactured using an incorrect rubber compound. Because of this, the tread on the tire can separate and detach from the tire itself, rather than remaining attached.

item.title: Mazda3 Rearview Mirror May Detach From Housing
item.description: On some Mazda3 cars equipped with a manual, non auto-dimming rearview mirror, the adhesive that bonds the mirror to its housing may not be properly applied. This can allow the mirror to detach and come off its mount while you are driving, leaving you without a rearview mirror to see what is behind you. Cars with auto-dimming mirrors are not affected by this issue.

item.title: Mazda3 front head restraints may not lock in place
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain Mazda3 cars. The seat cover material on both front seats can interfere with the button that releases the head restraint, the padded rest at the top of the seat back. The button can stick in the released position, which keeps the head restraint from locking into place and leaves it loose. Dealers will install spacers at the bottom of the release buttons on both front head restraints. There is no charge to the owner.

item.title: Mazda3, Mazda6 and CX-5 engines may stall unexpectedly
item.description: A software error in the computer that controls the engine may cause the engine to stall while the vehicle is being driven. Mazda dealers will reprogram that computer with corrected software at no charge. The recall began August 20, 2019, and owners can contact Mazda customer service to schedule the free repair.

item.title: Mazda3 Lug Nuts May Loosen, Wheel Could Detach
item.description: The lug nuts on all four wheels of certain Mazda3 vehicles may loosen. If this happens, a wheel could separate from the vehicle. A wheel separating from the vehicle increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Mazda CX-9 Wiring Fault Disables Airbag, Signals
item.description: Mazda says the wiring harness on some CX-9 SUVs can disrupt electrical connections. This may stop the passenger-side front airbag from working, cause the turn signals to fail, or prevent the engine from starting. These are separate possible effects of the same wiring problem, not something you would notice unless one of them happens on your vehicle.

item.title: Mazda3 Airbag and Seat Belt Warning Lights Wrong
item.description: Some 2019 Mazda3 vehicles have an indicator light problem caused by incorrect programming. The passenger airbag deactivation light may turn off even though the passenger airbag is actually deactivated. The seat belt warning lights for the front passenger and/or rear seats may also turn off even though those seat belts are unfastened.

item.title: Mazda3 windshield wipers may stop working from faulty relay
item.description: Mazda is recalling certain Mazda3 vehicles because of a faulty relay that controls the windshield wipers. A relay is the small switch that turns the wipers on and off. If it fails, the wipers can stop working altogether. Without working wipers, the driver's view through the windshield is reduced. Dealers will replace the body control module, the part that contains the relay, with a new one that uses an improved relay design.

item.title: Mazda MX-5 Transmission May Downshift Unexpectedly
item.description: In some Mazda MX-5 Miata vehicles with automatic transmissions, the computer that controls the transmission was programmed incorrectly. Under certain conditions, this can cause the vehicle to suddenly downshift on its own and abruptly slow down, without the driver choosing to do so.

item.title: Mazda CX-5 Side Curtain Airbags May Fail
item.description: In some Mazda CX-5 vehicles, the side curtain airbags may not fully unfold the way they are supposed to if the vehicle is in a side-impact crash or a rollover. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard meant to help keep passengers from being thrown from the vehicle during a crash. If the airbags don't work correctly, they may not protect occupants as intended.

item.title: Mazda3 Wrong Exhaust Valve Spring Can Stall Engine
item.description: Certain Mazda3 vehicles were built with an incorrect exhaust valve spring inside the engine. This spring may fail while the vehicle is being driven. If it fails, the engine can suddenly stall, meaning it shuts off while you are driving.
